title: Stack from an array
statement: Start simple: Build an integer stack with push, pop, and size. pop returns the most recently pushed value. Grow the backing storage when needed. The theory is optional. The C solution appears after the hidden tests pass.
constraints: pop on an empty stack throws IllegalStateException.
The last pushed value is the first returned.
think: A stack is a one-end structure.
The index after the last value is the top.
Push writes then advances; pop retreats then reads.
Growth is the same doubling idea as a dynamic array.
hints: Do not remove a hole in the middle.

tests.name: lifo
tests.call: { IntStack s = new IntStack(); s.push(1); s.push(2); return s.pop() + "," + s.pop(); }

tests.name: size
tests.call: { IntStack s = new IntStack(); s.push(4); s.push(5); return String.valueOf(s.size()); }

tests.name: after-pop
tests.call: { IntStack s = new IntStack(); s.push(4); s.pop(); return String.valueOf(s.size()); }

tests.name: reuse
tests.call: { IntStack s = new IntStack(); s.push(1); s.pop(); s.push(9); return String.valueOf(s.pop()); }

tests.name: many
tests.call: { IntStack s = new IntStack(); for (int i = 0; i < 30; i++) s.push(i); return s.pop() + ":" + s.size(); }

tests.name: zero
tests.call: { IntStack s = new IntStack(); s.push(0); return String.valueOf(s.pop()); }

objective: Implement push and pop around the next-free index while preserving LIFO order.
workedExample: After push(1), push(2), the next-free index is 2 and the top is at index 1.
Pop first decrements the index to 1, then reads index 1, so it returns 2 before 1.
recallPrompt: Why does pop retreat the top index before reading the value?

misconceptions.explanation: Reading the next-free slot skips the current top and can return an empty value.
misconceptions.retry: Mark the next-free index after two pushes, then mark the index pop should read.

misconceptions.explanation: An empty stack has no valid top index, so pop must reject it before reading.
misconceptions.retry: Write the empty-state check in plain language before writing the array access.

reflectionPrompt: State the stack invariant in one sentence and identify the operation that proves it.
